# HED task models

HED task models describe the tasks of behavioral and neuroimaging experiments in one
common framework, so that tasks run in different laboratories under different names can
be compared. The work is part of [HED](https://www.hedtags.org/) (Hierarchical Event
Descriptors), the standard for annotating what happened during an experiment, and the
values the models use are anchored on HED tags.

Two models work together.

- **The task model** treats every task as a game that the participant plays. A game
  is described by five things: its **game type**, its **game rules**, its **game
  motivators**, its **game phases** and its **game facets**. Two tasks described this
  way can be compared part by part, whatever they are called. See
  [The task model](task_model.md).
- **The cognitive process model** is a list of standard mental processes, each
  hypothesized to be engaged by one or more tasks, with the links between tasks and
  processes. See [The cognitive process model](process_model.md).

The starting point is a **task catalog** of {{ n_tasks }} traditional tasks, such as the
Stroop Color-Word Task, the N-Back Task and the Iowa Gambling Task, drawn from the
[Cognitive Atlas](https://www.cognitiveatlas.org/) and each modeled as a game, with
{{ n_variants }} variants and links to {{ n_processes }} cognitive processes. The next
step is to model the tasks of individual papers and datasets in the same terms;
[The modeling process](modeling_process.md) says how, and gives the template that is
filled in for a paper.

New here? Start with the [Introduction](introduction.md). To look up a task or to tag a
dataset, see [How to use the task catalog](how_to_use_the_catalog.md).

## Status and how to contribute

The task models are under development. The model itself, its vocabulary, the tasks and
the processes will all keep changing as more tasks are modeled, and identifiers are not
stable until a formal release. The initial work was done by Kay Robbins with the
assistance of Claude Opus 4 and, more recently, of Claude Fable 5, and is under review by
the [HED Working Group](https://www.hedtags.org/hed-resources) and other interested
parties.

Suggestions, corrections and ideas are welcome: please open an issue at
<https://github.com/hed-standard/hed-task/issues/new/choose>, where a form for a new
task, a new variant, a new process or a correction asks for what is needed. The
repository's
[contributing guide](https://github.com/hed-standard/hed-task/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
describes the process.

The pages under Related resources compare the task catalog, which those pages call the
Catalog, with two earlier resources: the
[Cognitive Atlas](atlas/the_catalog_vs_the_atlas.md) and the
[Cognitive Paradigm Ontology](cogpo/the_catalog_vs_cogpo.md) (CogPO).
